abstract: Countless studies have fitted Hodgkin-Huxley (HH) type models of active currents to voltage clamp data using nonlinear least squares. Yet, little is known about the uniqueness of parameter solutions and the interdependence of HH-type model parameters. Here, we show that considerable insight can be gained from the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a matrix closely related to the objective function used in the fitting procedure. After fitting all model parameters simultaneously using synthetic data originating from a representative range of experimental cases, this reveals that a manifold of solutions is possible depending on the type of voltage clamp data available and on the selected HH-type model. In such cases, we use the SVD to determine which parameters are least identifiable. Next, we develop an SVD-based manifold tracing technique that can efficiently unveil the structure of the manifold of equivalent solutions in the parameter space of the model. Our methods also identify parameter interdependencies and their impact on joint parameter confidence regions. The most salient one consistently observed across our experimental examples was between the peak conductance and reversal potential of active HH-type current models. The SVD-based strategy presented here is expected to be generally applicable to investigate parameter degeneracy and solution manifold structure in biophysical models of single neurons. Thus, our results should prove valuable for understanding the constraints imposed by the biophysics of ion channels on single neuron computation.
